-- Billing: subscription/lifetime-plan tracking + payment transaction log.
-- Plans themselves (name/price/period) live in code (src/lib/billing/plans.ts),
-- not the DB — fastest to ship, revisit if pricing needs to change without a
-- deploy. Only the current subscription STATE is in the DB (one row per
-- business, mutated in place, like `businesses` itself), plus an append-only
-- payment log for the Midtrans transaction history/audit trail.
--
-- Writes to both tables from the authenticated client are intentionally
-- narrow: a business can only ever INSERT a 'pending' payment (to kick off a
-- Midtrans transaction) and can only ever SELECT its own subscription state.
-- Every state transition (pending -> settlement, unpaid -> active, active ->
-- past_due -> expired) is written exclusively by the service-role Midtrans
-- webhook or the cron sweep, both of which bypass RLS entirely — so a
-- business can never mark its own subscription paid.
create table public.subscriptions (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  business_id uuid not null unique references public.businesses (id) on delete cascade,
  plan_code text not null,
  status text not null default 'unpaid'
    check (status in ('unpaid', 'active', 'past_due', 'expired')),
  period_end timestamptz, -- null = lifetime plan / never expires
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.subscriptions enable row level security;

create policy "Owner reads own subscription"
on public.subscriptions for select
using (private.owns_business(business_id));

create table public.payments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  business_id uuid not null references public.businesses (id) on delete cascade,
  plan_code text not null,
  order_id text not null unique,
  amount numeric(14, 2) not null check (amount > 0),
  status text not null default 'pending'
    check (status in ('pending', 'settlement', 'expire', 'cancel', 'deny')),
  midtrans_transaction_id text,
  payment_type text,
  raw_notification jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index payments_business_id_idx on public.payments (business_id, created_at desc);

alter table public.payments enable row level security;

create policy "Owner reads own payments"
on public.payments for select
using (private.owns_business(business_id));

create policy "Owner creates own pending payments"
on public.payments for insert
with check (private.owns_business(business_id) and status = 'pending');

-- Surface subscription status in the read-only /admin overview (see
-- [[mini-erp-scope]]-style follow-up pattern: small targeted redefinition of
-- an existing RPC, not a new admin billing back-office).
create or replace function public.admin_list_businesses()
returns table (
  id uuid,
  name text,
  business_type text,
  owner_email text,
  created_at timestamptz,
  shift_open boolean,
  tx_count bigint,
  subscription_status text,
  plan_code text
)
language plpgsql
security definer
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if not private.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorized';
  end if;

  return query
  select
    b.id,
    b.name,
    b.business_type,
    u.email::text,
    b.created_at,
    exists (select 1 from public.shifts s where s.business_id = b.id and s.closed_at is null),
    (
      coalesce((select count(*) from public.transactions t where t.business_id = b.id and not t.voided), 0)
      + coalesce((select count(*) from public.ticket_transactions tt where tt.business_id = b.id and not tt.voided), 0)
    ),
    coalesce(sub.status, 'unpaid'),
    nullif(sub.plan_code, '')
  from public.businesses b
  join auth.users u on u.id = b.owner_id
  left join public.subscriptions sub on sub.business_id = b.id
  order by b.created_at desc;
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.admin_list_businesses() to authenticated;

-- Surface subscription status in the read-only /admin overview (see
-- [[mini-erp-scope]]-style follow-up pattern: small targeted redefinition of
-- an existing RPC, not a new admin billing back-office).
create or replace function public.admin_list_businesses()
returns table (
  id uuid,
  name text,
  business_type text,
  owner_email text,
  created_at timestamptz,
  shift_open boolean,
  tx_count bigint,
  subscription_status text,
  plan_code text
)
language plpgsql
security definer
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if not private.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorized';
  end if;

  return query
  select
    b.id,
    b.name,
    b.business_type,
    u.email::text,
    b.created_at,
    exists (select 1 from public.shifts s where s.business_id = b.id and s.closed_at is null),
    (
      coalesce((select count(*) from public.transactions t where t.business_id = b.id and not t.voided), 0)
      + coalesce((select count(*) from public.ticket_transactions tt where tt.business_id = b.id and not tt.voided), 0)
    ),
    coalesce(sub.status, 'unpaid'),
    nullif(sub.plan_code, '')
  from public.businesses b
  join auth.users u on u.id = b.owner_id
  left join public.subscriptions sub on sub.business_id = b.id
  order by b.created_at desc;
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.admin_list_businesses() to authenticated;

Satu hal lagi yang saya butuh dari kamu untuk verifikasi penuh: **akun Midtrans (Sandbox)**. -- Surface subscription status in the read-only /admin overview (see
-- [[mini-erp-scope]]-style follow-up pattern: small targeted redefinition of
-- an existing RPC, not a new admin billing back-office).
create or replace function public.admin_list_businesses()
returns table (
  id uuid,
  name text,
  business_type text,
  owner_email text,
  created_at timestamptz,
  shift_open boolean,
  tx_count bigint,
  subscription_status text,
  plan_code text
)
language plpgsql
security definer
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if not private.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorized';
  end if;

  return query
  select
    b.id,
    b.name,
    b.business_type,
    u.email::text,
    b.created_at,
    exists (select 1 from public.shifts s where s.business_id = b.id and s.closed_at is null),
    (
      coalesce((select count(*) from public.transactions t where t.business_id = b.id and not t.voided), 0)
      + coalesce((select count(*) from public.ticket_transactions tt where tt.business_id = b.id and not tt.voided), 0)
    ),
    coalesce(sub.status, 'unpaid'),
    nullif(sub.plan_code, '')
  from public.businesses b
  join auth.users u on u.id = b.owner_id
  left join public.subscriptions sub on sub.business_id = b.id
  order by b.created_at desc;
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.admin_list_businesses() to authenticated;

Maksudnya nilai **`service_role` secret key** dari project Supabase kamu, bukan yang sudah ada. Cara ambilnya:

1. Buka dashboard Supabase project **KasirKu** kamu (yang sama seperti tab SQL Editor tadi)
2. Klik ikon **⚙️ Project Settings** (biasanya di pojok kiri bawah sidebar)
3. Masuk ke menu **API** (atau **API Keys**)
4. Di situ ada daftar **Project API keys** — ada 2 baris: `anon` `public` (itu yang sudah dipakai buat `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) dan **`service_role` `secret`**
5. Klik "Reveal"/mata di baris `service_role`, copy nilainya

Itu yang ditempel ke `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=` di [.env.local](.env.local:6) — **tempel langsung ke file-nya sendiri, jangan kirim ke saya di chat**, karena itu kunci yang bisa akses semua data tanpa batasan keamanan (RLS). Setelah disimpan, kabari saya saja "sudah" tanpa perlu kirim nilainya.
tidak ada tulisan reveal

Berarti project Supabase kamu pakai sistem API key baru. Di tab **"Publishable and secret API keys"** yang sedang kamu buka, scroll ke bawah — di bawah bagian "Publishable key" ada bagian **"Secret keys"** (bukan istilah "service_role" lagi, tapi fungsinya sama). Klik ikon mata/copy di situ untuk ambil nilainya (biasanya diawali `sb_secret_...`).

Kalau tetap tidak ketemu, coba klik tab sebelahnya **"Legacy anon, service_role API keys"** — di situ formatnya masih pakai istilah `service_role` yang lama dengan tombol reveal.

Ditempel ke file `.env.local` di project ini — **bukan ke saya di chat** (karena itu kunci rahasia yang bisa akses semua data tanpa batasan).

Caranya:
1. Buka File Explorer, masuk ke folder `G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu`
2. Cari file bernama **`.env.local`** (file tersembunyi/dot-file — kalau tidak kelihatan, aktifkan "Show hidden files" di File Explorer, atau buka pakai VS Code/Notepad langsung lewat "Open With")
3. Buka dengan Notepad (klik kanan → Open with → Notepad, atau VS Code kalau ada)
4. Cari baris `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=`
5. Tempel (paste) nilai yang tadi di-copy, persis setelah tanda `=` (tanpa spasi)
6. Save (Ctrl+S)

Setelah itu kabari saya "sudah" — saya lanjut testing.

content.text:
Semua terverifikasi lengkap. Ringkasan hasil testing end-to-end:

**Yang sudah terbukti bekerja (tanpa perlu kunci Midtrans asli):**
- ✅ Toko lama (existing) tetap bisa diakses — backfill/grandfather berhasil
- ✅ Signup baru → langsung diarahkan ke `/billing`, tidak bisa ke dashboard/POS sebelum bayar
- ✅ Tombol "Bayar Sekarang" benar membuat baris `payments` dan memanggil API Midtrans (gagal karena kunci dummy, itu memang diharapkan)
- ✅ Webhook Midtrans: verifikasi signature benar, `payments.status` → `settlement`, `subscriptions.status` → `active`, `period_end = null` untuk paket lifetime
- ✅ Dashboard & POS terbuka otomatis setelah "pembayaran" masuk
- ✅ Cron sweep: `active` (lewat jatuh tempo) → `past_due` (banner peringatan muncul, akses tetap jalan) → `expired` (dikunci lagi, redirect ke `/billing`) — persis sesuai keputusan masa tenggang 3 hari
- ✅ Keamanan: webhook menolak signature salah (401), cron menolak tanpa/salah secret (403)

**Bug yang saya temukan & perbaiki di tengah testing:** middleware ternyata me-redirect endpoint `/api/midtrans/notification` dan `/api/cron/*` ke `/login` karena dianggap butuh sesi login — padahal keduanya dipanggil server-to-server oleh Midtrans/Vercel tanpa sesi browser sama sekali. Sudah diperbaiki di [middleware.ts](src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts:47).

**Yang masih perlu sebelum benar-benar live:**
1. Ganti `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY` di `.env.local` dengan kunci **Sandbox** asli dari dashboard Midtrans (nilai sekarang cuma dummy untuk testing saya) — biar bisa coba redirect ke halaman bayar Midtrans sungguhan
2. Set semua env var billing (`MIDTRANS_*`, `CRON_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) juga di pengaturan environment Vercel saat deploy
3. Daftarkan URL webhook `https://<domain-kamu>/api/midtrans/notification` di dashboard Midtrans (menu Settings → Configuration → Payment Notification URL)
4. Setelah puas dengan Sandbox, ganti ke kunci production + `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=true`

Semua kode sudah lint & type-check bersih, dan belum di-commit — mau saya commit sekarang?

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add Midtrans billing: subscription + lifetime plans

KasirKu had no way for a business owner to pay for the product at all —
this adds the missing piece before public launch. New businesses must
pick and pay for a plan (monthly/yearly subscription or a one-time
lifetime purchase) immediately after signup before the dashboard or POS
is usable; a lapsed subscription gets a 3-day grace period with a
warning banner before locking out. Existing businesses are grandfathered
with permanent free access so this doesn't disrupt current tenants.

- New `subscriptions`/`payments` tables, RLS-gated so only the
  service-role Midtrans webhook/cron sweep can ever mark a business paid
- Billing page + Midtrans Snap checkout, webhook with signature
  verification, daily cron to age active -> past_due -> expired
- Admin panel now surfaces each tenant's subscription status
- Fixed a middleware bug found during testing: /api/midtrans and
  /api/cron were being redirected to /login since they're server-to-server
  endpoints with no browser session

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
git status --short

---
name: billing-midtrans
description: Midtrans subscription + lifetime-purchase billing system — schema, gating, webhook, cron, and E2E test results
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1481b9c4-7ecb-4dcd-9555-68f50a4188ce
---

Built 2026-07-12, closing the #1 launch blocker identified in a full codebase audit (see [[project-purpose-saas-product]]): before this, there was no way for anyone to pay for KasirKu at all. User's decisions that shaped the design: both a recurring subscription AND a one-time lifetime purchase (not subscription-only), **Midtrans** as the gateway, **no trial** (must pick+pay immediately after signup), and a **3-day grace period** (past_due banner) before a lapsed subscription actually locks the account out.

**Schema** (migrations `20260712110000_billing.sql` + `20260712120000_admin_billing_columns.sql`): `public.subscriptions` (one row per business, mutated in place — `status` unpaid/active/past_due/expired, `plan_code`, `period_end` null=lifetime) and `public.payments` (append-only Midtrans transaction log). RLS is deliberately narrow: a business can SELECT its own rows and INSERT exactly one `unpaid` subscription (at onboarding) / any number of `pending` payments (to start a Midtrans transaction) — but can never write `active`/`settlement`/etc itself. Only the service-role Midtrans webhook and cron sweep can transition status, so a tenant can never mark itself paid. Plan catalog (name/price/period) is a **TS constant** (`src/lib/billing/plans.ts`), not DB-driven — fast to ship, revisit if pricing needs to change without a deploy. **Prices are placeholders** (Rp99rb/bulan, Rp990rb/tahun, Rp2,5jt lifetime) — must be edited before real launch, no real pricing input was given.

**Existing businesses were grandfathered** — the billing migration backfills every pre-existing business with a permanent `active`/`lifetime`/`period_end=null` subscription row, so toko-toko test yang sudah ada tidak mendadak terkunci begitu migrasi jalan. This was almost missed — caught before applying the migration, not after.

**Enforcement**: two independent Server Component layouts do the actual lockout — `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and a new `pos/layout.tsx` — both call `getSubscriptionAccess()` (`src/lib/billing/status.ts`) and `redirect()` to `/business/<id>/billing` if locked (`unpaid`/`expired`). Deliberately NOT one shared `[businessId]/layout.tsx` wrapping everything, since that would redirect-loop on the billing page itself (Next.js layouts can't easily detect "am I currently the billing page"). `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` also shows a past_due warning banner (amber, in `dashboard-shell.tsx`) with a link to `/billing` — pos doesn't need the banner, cashiers don't need to see billing state.

**Payment flow**: `billing/actions.ts` `createPayment()` inserts a `pending` payment row, then calls Midtrans Snap's create-transaction API (sandbox vs production host picked via `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION`), returns a `redirect_url` the client does a plain `window.location.href` to (no Snap.js popup SDK). Webhook at `src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts` verifies the `sha512(order_id+status_code+gross_amount+MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY)` signature, uses a **new service-role Supabase client** (`src/lib/supabase/service.ts` — first use of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in this codebase, only ever import this in the webhook/cron, never in user-facing code), flips `payments.status` and (idempotently — checks for already-`settlement` first) activates the subscription, extending `period_end` from the greater of now-or-existing-period_end (so early renewal doesn't lose paid days). Daily cron (`vercel.json` + `src/app/api/cron/subscription-sweep/route.ts`, guarded by `CRON_SECRET` bearer header) ages `active`→`past_due` (period_end passed) →`expired` (past_due + 3 days).

**Bug found and fixed during E2E testing**: `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s public-path allowlist didn't exempt `/api/*` routes, so Midtrans's webhook and Vercel's cron caller — both server-to-server with zero browser session — were being redirected to `/login` instead of reaching the route handler at all. Fixed by adding `/api/midtrans` and `/api/cron` to `isPublicPath`. Caught by literally curling the webhook locally and getting back the string `/login` instead of JSON — a good reminder to always hit new API routes with a bare curl (no cookies) as part of verifying them, not just through the browser (which carries a session and would have masked this).

**Verified E2E 2026-07-12, all without needing real Midtrans credentials** (used a locally-set dummy `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`CRON_SECRET` in `.env.local` just to exercise the signature/auth logic, plus a Node script using the real `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to backdate `period_end` directly via the REST API since RLS blocks the owner from writing to `subscriptions` themselves):
- Existing "Toko Test Laporan" stayed fully accessible after the migration (grandfather confirmed).
- Fresh signup → onboarding → landed on `/billing` (not `/dashboard`), status "Belum Berlangganan"; direct URL access to both the dashboard and `/pos` correctly redirected back to `/billing`.
- Clicked "Bayar Sekarang" (lifetime plan) → pending payment row created, Midtrans rejected the fake key with a real API error surfaced cleanly in the UI (confirms the actual HTTP call shape is correct, just needs real Sandbox keys next).
- Hand-crafted a correctly-signed `settlement` webhook payload (order_id pulled via a REST call using the browser's own session cookie, signature computed with Node's `crypto`) → `payments.status` → `settlement`, `subscriptions.status` → `active`, `plan_code` → `lifetime`, `period_end` → `null`. Dashboard unlocked immediately after.
- Cron sweep: backdated an `active` monthly subscription's `period_end` to yesterday → sweep flipped it to `past_due` (dashboard still reachable, amber banner present, confirmed via `document.body.innerText.includes(...)` since the banner sits outside `<main>` and `get_page_text` only grabs `<main>`). Backdated further to 4 days past → sweep flipped to `expired` → dashboard redirected to `/billing` again, showing "Kedaluwarsa".
- Security: webhook with a wrong `signature_key` → 401. Cron with no/wrong `Authorization` header → 403.

**Still needed before this can go actually live** (not done, no real credentials available this session): real Midtrans Sandbox `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY` in `.env.local` to test the real Snap-hosted checkout redirect; the same billing env vars set in Vercel's environment settings for deploy; the webhook URL (`https://<domain>/api/midtrans/notification`) registered in the Midtrans dashboard's payment notification settings; then swap to production keys + `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=true` when ready. Also no admin UI yet to manually comp/override a tenant's billing status (e.g. for an offline bank-transfer edge case) — flagged as a fast-follow, not built.

**Postgres gotcha hit while migrating**: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` fails with `42P13 cannot change return type of existing function` when you add new OUT-parameter columns to a `RETURNS TABLE(...)` function (here, extending `admin_list_businesses()` with `subscription_status`/`plan_code`). Fix is `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS ... ; CREATE FUNCTION ...` instead of `CREATE OR REPLACE` — worth remembering for any future RPC signature change, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]].

content.text:
Uangnya **tidak langsung masuk ke rekening kamu otomatis** — ada beberapa langkah dulu:

## Alurnya

1. **Pelanggan bayar** (lewat VA, e-wallet, QRIS, kartu, dll) → uangnya masuk ke **saldo Midtrans** kamu dulu, bukan langsung ke rekening bank.
2. **Midtrans potong biaya transaksi** (beda-beda per metode, contoh kasar: QRIS ~0,7%, VA ~Rp4rb flat, kartu kredit ~2,9%+Rp2rb).
3. **Midtrans "settle" (transfer) ke rekening bank kamu** secara berkala — biasanya H+1 sampai H+7 hari kerja tergantung metode bayar & jenis akun merchant kamu.

## Yang perlu kamu siapkan supaya uangnya benar-benar bisa cair ke rekeningmu

1. **Daftar akun Midtrans asli** di midtrans.com (bukan cuma ambil kunci Sandbox) — ini beda dari sekadar bikin akun, ada proses **verifikasi bisnis (KYC)**: biasanya perlu KTP, NPWP, dan kalau usaha berbadan (PT/CV) dokumen pendiriannya. Bisa juga daftar sebagai perorangan/UMKM.
2. **Daftarkan rekening bank kamu** di dashboard Midtrans (menu Settlement/Payout) — ini rekening tujuan uang hasil transaksi akan ditransfer.
3. Selama masih pakai **kunci Sandbox**, semua ini simulasi doang — tidak ada uang sungguhan bergerak, aman buat testing.
4. Baru setelah verifikasi bisnis selesai dan kamu dapat **kunci Production**, transaksi jadi sungguhan dan uang beneran mengalir ke rekeningmu sesuai jadwal settlement itu.

**Penting:** kunci `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`CRON_SECRET` yang saya isi di `.env.local` kemarin itu **cuma nilai dummy buatan saya sendiri** untuk uji logika kode (bukan kunci asli dari akun Midtrans manapun) — jadi belum ada koneksi ke uang sungguhan sama sekali saat ini.

Mau saya bantu apa selanjutnya — misalnya jelasin langkah daftar akun Midtrans real, atau ada bagian lain dari alur ini yang masih membingungkan?

Itu checkbox **"Bisnis saya menggunakan web developer."** — pertanyaannya kira-kira: apakah bisnismu pakai jasa web developer (internal/eksternal) untuk mengelola sisi teknis integrasi pembayarannya.

Kemungkinan besar kalau dicentang, form akan minta detail tambahan (nama/kontak developer) sebagai PIC teknis integrasi API Midtrans-nya.

Karena kamu sendiri yang membangun KasirKu (dengan bantuan saya untuk coding), kamu **secara teknis punya developer** (dirimu sendiri, atau bisa juga dianggap "developer eksternal" kalau mau mencantumkan tim/kontak teknis terpisah). Rekomendasi saya:

- **Kalau kamu tetap yang pegang kendali penuh** (isi kunci, pasang di kode, dsb — seperti yang kita lakukan sekarang) → boleh **dicentang** dan isi datamu sendiri sebagai kontak teknis, supaya kalau ada masalah integrasi API, Midtrans tahu harus menghubungi siapa.
- **Kalau mau lebih simpel dan tidak ada developer terpisah yang perlu didaftarkan** → **tidak usah dicentang**, lanjut saja ke kolom lain.

Tidak ada jawaban yang "salah" di sini — ini cuma soal kelengkapan data kontak. Kalau kamu centang dan muncul kolom tambahan, kirim screenshot-nya, saya bantu isi lanjutannya.

Di dashboard Midtrans yang lebih baru ini (namanya "MAP"), Sandbox dan Production kadang sudah tidak dipisah jadi 2 URL dashboard berbeda seperti versi lama Midtrans — jadi saya tidak bisa pastikan 100% dari screenshot ini apakah kunci yang ditampilkan itu sudah otomatis bisa dipakai buat testing (Sandbox-mode) atau baru aktif kalau statusnya sudah "aktif" penuh (2-3 hari lagi).

Tapi ada cara paling gampang buat mastiin: **langsung dicoba saja**, karena testing di server Sandbox Midtrans **tidak akan pernah memindahkan uang sungguhan**, apapun hasilnya:

1. Tempel `Server Key` dan `Client Key` yang tadi kamu screenshot ke `.env.local` (ganti nilai dummy kemarin), pastikan `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=false`
2. Kabari saya "sudah"
3. Saya coba tombol "Bayar Sekarang" di halaman billing KasirKu → kalau Midtrans terima, berarti kunci itu memang jalan buat testing sekarang juga (tidak perlu nunggu approval 2-3 hari). Kalau ditolak dengan pesan semacam "merchant belum aktif", berarti memang harus nunggu approval dulu.

Cara ini aman dicoba kapan saja karena request ke server sandbox Midtrans (`app.sandbox.midtrans.com`) tidak pernah menyentuh uang asli.

Tidak, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` **jangan diubah** — itu sudah benar, sudah diisi sebelumnya (kunci Supabase, tidak ada hubungannya sama Midtrans).

Yang perlu diganti sekarang cuma 2 baris ini:

```
MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY=local-test-server-key-not-real
MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY=
```

Ganti nilai `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY` (yang sekarang masih dummy) dan isi `MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY` (yang masih kosong) dengan Server Key dan Client Key asli dari Midtrans yang tadi kamu screenshot. Baris `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` dan `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=false` biarkan seperti sekarang.

content.text:
Sudah kebaca kuncinya, tapi Midtrans tetap menolak dengan pesan yang sama: **"Access denied due to unauthorized transaction, please check client or server key"**.

Ini artinya kemungkinan besar akun kamu **belum bisa dipakai untuk transaksi sama sekali** (baik sandbox maupun production) selama status masih "Dalam proses" — beda dari dugaan saya sebelumnya. Sepertinya di sistem onboarding Midtrans yang baru ("MAP") ini, kunci baru benar-benar aktif setelah review 2-3 hari kerja selesai, tidak ada mode testing instan.

Ada 2 opsi:

1. **Tunggu 2-3 hari kerja** sampai review selesai, baru kita coba lagi dengan kunci yang sama.
2. **Coba akun Sandbox klasik terpisah** — dulu Midtrans punya sistem lama di `dashboard.sandbox.midtrans.com` yang bisa langsung dipakai testing tanpa perlu verifikasi bisnis sama sekali (akun testing yang benar-benar terpisah dari akun bisnis asli). Kalau kamu buka link itu dan masih bisa daftar/masuk, kita bisa dapat kunci testing instan dari situ.

Mau coba opsi 2 dulu (buka `dashboard.sandbox.midtrans.com`), atau tunggu saja review-nya kelar?

Oke, coba ini di tab Chrome kamu sendiri (bukan yang saya buka):

1. Buka **https://dashboard.sandbox.midtrans.com/**
2. Kalau muncul halaman login/daftar — ini akun **terpisah** dari akun bisnis Midtrans yang tadi kamu daftarkan, jadi kemungkinan perlu **daftar baru** (register) khusus untuk sandbox, bisa pakai email yang sama
3. Proses daftarnya biasanya **instan, tanpa verifikasi bisnis/KYC** — karena memang cuma buat testing, bukan buat terima uang sungguhan
4. Setelah masuk, cari menu **Settings → Access Keys** (sama seperti yang tadi)
5. Kuncinya di situ biasanya berawalan **`SB-Mid-server-...`** dan **`SB-Mid-client-...`** (ada prefix "SB-" yang menandakan Sandbox)

Kirim screenshot kalau sudah sampai halaman itu, saya bantu pandu lanjutannya.

---
name: billing-midtrans
description: Midtrans subscription + lifetime-purchase billing system — schema, gating, webhook, cron, and E2E test results
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1481b9c4-7ecb-4dcd-9555-68f50a4188ce
---

Built 2026-07-12, closing the #1 launch blocker identified in a full codebase audit (see [[project-purpose-saas-product]]): before this, there was no way for anyone to pay for KasirKu at all. User's decisions that shaped the design: both a recurring subscription AND a one-time lifetime purchase (not subscription-only), **Midtrans** as the gateway, **no trial** (must pick+pay immediately after signup), and a **3-day grace period** (past_due banner) before a lapsed subscription actually locks the account out.

**Schema** (migrations `20260712110000_billing.sql` + `20260712120000_admin_billing_columns.sql`): `public.subscriptions` (one row per business, mutated in place — `status` unpaid/active/past_due/expired, `plan_code`, `period_end` null=lifetime) and `public.payments` (append-only Midtrans transaction log). RLS is deliberately narrow: a business can SELECT its own rows and INSERT exactly one `unpaid` subscription (at onboarding) / any number of `pending` payments (to start a Midtrans transaction) — but can never write `active`/`settlement`/etc itself. Only the service-role Midtrans webhook and cron sweep can transition status, so a tenant can never mark itself paid. Plan catalog (name/price/period) is a **TS constant** (`src/lib/billing/plans.ts`), not DB-driven — fast to ship, revisit if pricing needs to change without a deploy. **Prices are placeholders** (Rp99rb/bulan, Rp990rb/tahun, Rp2,5jt lifetime) — must be edited before real launch, no real pricing input was given.

**Existing businesses were grandfathered** — the billing migration backfills every pre-existing business with a permanent `active`/`lifetime`/`period_end=null` subscription row, so toko-toko test yang sudah ada tidak mendadak terkunci begitu migrasi jalan. This was almost missed — caught before applying the migration, not after.

**Enforcement**: two independent Server Component layouts do the actual lockout — `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and a new `pos/layout.tsx` — both call `getSubscriptionAccess()` (`src/lib/billing/status.ts`) and `redirect()` to `/business/<id>/billing` if locked (`unpaid`/`expired`). Deliberately NOT one shared `[businessId]/layout.tsx` wrapping everything, since that would redirect-loop on the billing page itself (Next.js layouts can't easily detect "am I currently the billing page"). `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` also shows a past_due warning banner (amber, in `dashboard-shell.tsx`) with a link to `/billing` — pos doesn't need the banner, cashiers don't need to see billing state.

**Payment flow**: `billing/actions.ts` `createPayment()` inserts a `pending` payment row, then calls Midtrans Snap's create-transaction API (sandbox vs production host picked via `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION`), returns a `redirect_url` the client does a plain `window.location.href` to (no Snap.js popup SDK). Webhook at `src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts` verifies the `sha512(order_id+status_code+gross_amount+MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY)` signature, uses a **new service-role Supabase client** (`src/lib/supabase/service.ts` — first use of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in this codebase, only ever import this in the webhook/cron, never in user-facing code), flips `payments.status` and (idempotently — checks for already-`settlement` first) activates the subscription, extending `period_end` from the greater of now-or-existing-period_end (so early renewal doesn't lose paid days). Daily cron (`vercel.json` + `src/app/api/cron/subscription-sweep/route.ts`, guarded by `CRON_SECRET` bearer header) ages `active`→`past_due` (period_end passed) →`expired` (past_due + 3 days).

**Bug found and fixed during E2E testing**: `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s public-path allowlist didn't exempt `/api/*` routes, so Midtrans's webhook and Vercel's cron caller — both server-to-server with zero browser session — were being redirected to `/login` instead of reaching the route handler at all. Fixed by adding `/api/midtrans` and `/api/cron` to `isPublicPath`. Caught by literally curling the webhook locally and getting back the string `/login` instead of JSON — a good reminder to always hit new API routes with a bare curl (no cookies) as part of verifying them, not just through the browser (which carries a session and would have masked this).

**Verified E2E 2026-07-12, all without needing real Midtrans credentials** (used a locally-set dummy `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`CRON_SECRET` in `.env.local` just to exercise the signature/auth logic, plus a Node script using the real `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to backdate `period_end` directly via the REST API since RLS blocks the owner from writing to `subscriptions` themselves):
- Existing "Toko Test Laporan" stayed fully accessible after the migration (grandfather confirmed).
- Fresh signup → onboarding → landed on `/billing` (not `/dashboard`), status "Belum Berlangganan"; direct URL access to both the dashboard and `/pos` correctly redirected back to `/billing`.
- Clicked "Bayar Sekarang" (lifetime plan) → pending payment row created, Midtrans rejected the fake key with a real API error surfaced cleanly in the UI (confirms the actual HTTP call shape is correct, just needs real Sandbox keys next).
- Hand-crafted a correctly-signed `settlement` webhook payload (order_id pulled via a REST call using the browser's own session cookie, signature computed with Node's `crypto`) → `payments.status` → `settlement`, `subscriptions.status` → `active`, `plan_code` → `lifetime`, `period_end` → `null`. Dashboard unlocked immediately after.
- Cron sweep: backdated an `active` monthly subscription's `period_end` to yesterday → sweep flipped it to `past_due` (dashboard still reachable, amber banner present, confirmed via `document.body.innerText.includes(...)` since the banner sits outside `<main>` and `get_page_text` only grabs `<main>`). Backdated further to 4 days past → sweep flipped to `expired` → dashboard redirected to `/billing` again, showing "Kedaluwarsa".
- Security: webhook with a wrong `signature_key` → 401. Cron with no/wrong `Authorization` header → 403.

**Still needed before this can go actually live** (not done, no real credentials available this session): real Midtrans Sandbox `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY` in `.env.local` to test the real Snap-hosted checkout redirect; the same billing env vars set in Vercel's environment settings for deploy; the webhook URL (`https://<domain>/api/midtrans/notification`) registered in the Midtrans dashboard's payment notification settings; then swap to production keys + `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=true` when ready. Also no admin UI yet to manually comp/override a tenant's billing status (e.g. for an offline bank-transfer edge case) — flagged as a fast-follow, not built.

**Postgres gotcha hit while migrating**: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` fails with `42P13 cannot change return type of existing function` when you add new OUT-parameter columns to a `RETURNS TABLE(...)` function (here, extending `admin_list_businesses()` with `subscription_status`/`plan_code`). Ini poin penting yang memang belum saya bangun — jujur saja, **saat ini belum ada cara untuk mengaktifkan langganan pelanggan yang bayar manual (transfer/WA)**. Biar jelas kenapa:

## Kenapa ini jadi masalah sekarang

Sistem yang saya bangun kemarin cuma punya 2 jalan untuk mengubah status langganan jadi "Aktif":
1. **Webhook Midtrans** — otomatis, tapi ini belum aktif karena akun Midtrans-mu masih direview
2. **Cron harian** — cuma jalan untuk mengunci akun yang telat bayar, bukan mengaktifkan

Jadi kalau pelanggan transfer manual dan chat kamu di WhatsApp, **tidak ada tombol atau halaman di aplikasi buat kamu bilang "oke, orang ini sudah bayar, buka aksesnya"**. Sengaja saya desain begitu supaya pelanggan sendiri tidak bisa curang mengaktifkan langganannya sendiri (cuma sistem/admin yang boleh) — tapi saya lupa sediakan alat untuk kamu sebagai admin melakukan itu secara manual.

## Solusinya

Saya perlu tambahkan fitur kecil di panel **`/admin`** (yang cuma bisa kamu akses): tiap toko ada tombol **"Tandai Sudah Bayar"** — kamu pilih paketnya (Bulanan/Tahunan/Lifetime), klik, dan sistem otomatis:
- Mencatat pembayaran itu di riwayat (sebagai "manual", biar ketahuan beda dari pembayaran via Midtrans)
- Mengaktifkan langganan toko itu, hitung tanggal berlakunya

Setelah itu, pelanggan yang tadi transfer bisa langsung buka dashboard/kasirnya lagi.

Mau saya bangunkan fitur ini sekarang?

-- Manual activation path for /admin: while Midtrans is offline/unverified
-- (or for any future offline bank-transfer case), the superadmin needs a way
-- to mark a business as paid after confirming payment themselves — see
-- [[billing-midtrans]]. Business logic mirrors the webhook's activation
-- exactly (src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts): extend from the
-- greater of now() or the existing period_end so an early renewal doesn't
-- lose paid-for days; p_period_days null means a lifetime plan (never
-- expires). Records a 'manual' payment row for the same audit trail the
-- Midtrans webhook produces, just tagged differently.
create or replace function public.admin_activate_subscription(
  p_business_id uuid,
  p_plan_code text,
  p_period_days int,
  p_amount numeric,
  p_note text default null
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  v_current_period_end timestamptz;
  v_new_period_end timestamptz;
begin
  if not private.is_admin() then
    raise exception 'not authorized';
  end if;

  if p_amount is null or p_amount <= 0 then
    raise exception 'amount must be positive';
  end if;

  select period_end into v_current_period_end
  from public.subscriptions
  where business_id = p_business_id;

  if p_period_days is null then
    v_new_period_end := null;
  else
    v_new_period_end := greatest(now(), coalesce(v_current_period_end, now()))
      + (p_period_days || ' days')::interval;
  end if;

  insert into public.payments (
    business_id, plan_code, order_id, amount, status, payment_type, raw_notification
  )
  values (
    p_business_id,
    p_plan_code,
    'MANUAL-' || replace(p_business_id::text, '-', '') || '-' || floor(extract(epoch from now()))::text,
    p_amount,
    'settlement',
    'manual',
    jsonb_build_object('note', p_note, 'activated_by', 'admin')
  );

  insert into public.subscriptions (business_id, plan_code, status, period_end, updated_at)
  values (p_business_id, p_plan_code, 'active', v_new_period_end, now())
  on conflict (business_id) do update set
    plan_code = excluded.plan_code,
    status = 'active',
    period_end = excluded.period_end,
    updated_at = now();
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.admin_activate_subscription(uuid, text, int, numeric, text) to authenticated;

  where business_id = p_business_id;

  if p_period_days is null then
    v_new_period_end := null;
  else
    v_new_period_end := greatest(now(), coalesce(v_current_period_end, now()))
      + (p_period_days || ' days')::interval;
  end if;

  insert into public.payments (
    business_id, plan_code, order_id, amount, status, payment_type, raw_notification
  )
  values (
    p_business_id,
    p_plan_code,
    'MANUAL-' || replace(p_business_id::text, '-', '') || '-' || floor(extract(epoch from now()))::text,
    p_amount,
    'settlement',
    'manual',
    jsonb_build_object('note', p_note, 'activated_by', 'admin')
  );

  insert into public.subscriptions (business_id, plan_code, status, period_end, updated_at)
  values (p_business_id, p_plan_code, 'active', v_new_period_end, now())
  on conflict (business_id) do update set
    plan_code = excluded.plan_code,
    status = 'active',
    period_end = excluded.period_end,
    updated_at = now();
end;
$$;

name: billing-midtrans
description: Midtrans subscription + lifetime-purchase billing system — schema, gating, webhook, cron, and E2E test results
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1481b9c4-7ecb-4dcd-9555-68f50a4188ce
---

Built 2026-07-12, closing the #1 launch blocker identified in a full codebase audit (see [[project-purpose-saas-product]]): before this, there was no way for anyone to pay for KasirKu at all. User's decisions that shaped the design: both a recurring subscription AND a one-time lifetime purchase (not subscription-only), **Midtrans** as the gateway, **no trial** (must pick+pay immediately after signup), and a **3-day grace period** (past_due banner) before a lapsed subscription actually locks the account out.

**Schema** (migrations `20260712110000_billing.sql` + `20260712120000_admin_billing_columns.sql`): `public.subscriptions` (one row per business, mutated in place — `status` unpaid/active/past_due/expired, `plan_code`, `period_end` null=lifetime) and `public.payments` (append-only Midtrans transaction log). RLS is deliberately narrow: a business can SELECT its own rows and INSERT exactly one `unpaid` subscription (at onboarding) / any number of `pending` payments (to start a Midtrans transaction) — but can never write `active`/`settlement`/etc itself. Only the service-role Midtrans webhook and cron sweep can transition status, so a tenant can never mark itself paid. Plan catalog (name/price/period) is a **TS constant** (`src/lib/billing/plans.ts`), not DB-driven — fast to ship, revisit if pricing needs to change without a deploy. **Prices are placeholders** (Rp99rb/bulan, Rp990rb/tahun, Rp2,5jt lifetime) — must be edited before real launch, no real pricing input was given.

**Existing businesses were grandfathered** — the billing migration backfills every pre-existing business with a permanent `active`/`lifetime`/`period_end=null` subscription row, so toko-toko test yang sudah ada tidak mendadak terkunci begitu migrasi jalan. This was almost missed — caught before applying the migration, not after.

**Enforcement**: two independent Server Component layouts do the actual lockout — `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and a new `pos/layout.tsx` — both call `getSubscriptionAccess()` (`src/lib/billing/status.ts`) and `redirect()` to `/business/<id>/billing` if locked (`unpaid`/`expired`). Deliberately NOT one shared `[businessId]/layout.tsx` wrapping everything, since that would redirect-loop on the billing page itself (Next.js layouts can't easily detect "am I currently the billing page"). `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` also shows a past_due warning banner (amber, in `dashboard-shell.tsx`) with a link to `/billing` — pos doesn't need the banner, cashiers don't need to see billing state.

**Payment flow**: `billing/actions.ts` `createPayment()` inserts a `pending` payment row, then calls Midtrans Snap's create-transaction API (sandbox vs production host picked via `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION`), returns a `redirect_url` the client does a plain `window.location.href` to (no Snap.js popup SDK). Webhook at `src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts` verifies the `sha512(order_id+status_code+gross_amount+MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY)` signature, uses a **new service-role Supabase client** (`src/lib/supabase/service.ts` — first use of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in this codebase, only ever import this in the webhook/cron, never in user-facing code), flips `payments.status` and (idempotently — checks for already-`settlement` first) activates the subscription, extending `period_end` from the greater of now-or-existing-period_end (so early renewal doesn't lose paid days). Daily cron (`vercel.json` + `src/app/api/cron/subscription-sweep/route.ts`, guarded by `CRON_SECRET` bearer header) ages `active`→`past_due` (period_end passed) →`expired` (past_due + 3 days).

**Bug found and fixed during E2E testing**: `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`'s public-path allowlist didn't exempt `/api/*` routes, so Midtrans's webhook and Vercel's cron caller — both server-to-server with zero browser session — were being redirected to `/login` instead of reaching the route handler at all. Fixed by adding `/api/midtrans` and `/api/cron` to `isPublicPath`. Caught by literally curling the webhook locally and getting back the string `/login` instead of JSON — a good reminder to always hit new API routes with a bare curl (no cookies) as part of verifying them, not just through the browser (which carries a session and would have masked this).

**Verified E2E 2026-07-12, all without needing real Midtrans credentials** (used a locally-set dummy `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`CRON_SECRET` in `.env.local` just to exercise the signature/auth logic, plus a Node script using the real `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` to backdate `period_end` directly via the REST API since RLS blocks the owner from writing to `subscriptions` themselves):
- Existing "Toko Test Laporan" stayed fully accessible after the migration (grandfather confirmed).
- Fresh signup → onboarding → landed on `/billing` (not `/dashboard`), status "Belum Berlangganan"; direct URL access to both the dashboard and `/pos` correctly redirected back to `/billing`.
- Clicked "Bayar Sekarang" (lifetime plan) → pending payment row created, Midtrans rejected the fake key with a real API error surfaced cleanly in the UI (confirms the actual HTTP call shape is correct, just needs real Sandbox keys next).
- Hand-crafted a correctly-signed `settlement` webhook payload (order_id pulled via a REST call using the browser's own session cookie, signature computed with Node's `crypto`) → `payments.status` → `settlement`, `subscriptions.status` → `active`, `plan_code` → `lifetime`, `period_end` → `null`. Dashboard unlocked immediately after.
- Cron sweep: backdated an `active` monthly subscription's `period_end` to yesterday → sweep flipped it to `past_due` (dashboard still reachable, amber banner present, confirmed via `document.body.innerText.includes(...)` since the banner sits outside `<main>` and `get_page_text` only grabs `<main>`). Backdated further to 4 days past → sweep flipped to `expired` → dashboard redirected to `/billing` again, showing "Kedaluwarsa".
- Security: webhook with a wrong `signature_key` → 401. Cron with no/wrong `Authorization` header → 403.

**Still needed before this can go actually live** (not done, no real credentials available this session): real Midtrans Sandbox `MIDTRANS_SERVER_KEY`/`MIDTRANS_CLIENT_KEY` in `.env.local` to test the real Snap-hosted checkout redirect; the same billing env vars set in Vercel's environment settings for deploy; the webhook URL (`https://<domain>/api/midtrans/notification`) registered in the Midtrans dashboard's payment notification settings; then swap to production keys + `MIDTRANS_IS_PRODUCTION=true` when ready. Also no admin UI yet to manually comp/override a tenant's billing status (e.g. for an offline bank-transfer edge case) — flagged as a fast-follow, not built.

**Update 2026-07-12, same day**: user registered a real Midtrans business account ("Createimpact.id", perorangan) via the newer unified "MAP" onboarding at passport.midtrans.com — business verification came back "Dalam proses, aktif dalam 2-3 hari kerja" (not instant). Tried the account's Access Key page (`dashboard.midtrans.com/settings/access-keys`) keys anyway against our Sandbox API host — Midtrans rejected with "Access denied due to unauthorized transaction, please check client or server key", confirming this newer onboarding flow does NOT give you working Sandbox-testable keys immediately; both sandbox and production calls are gated behind the same verification. User chose to skip waiting on it for now rather than try the old separate `dashboard.sandbox.midtrans.com` classic-sandbox route.
- **Interim solution built**: `src/lib/billing/config.ts` — `BILLING_MANUAL_MODE` (currently `true`) + `BILLING_CONTACT` (WhatsApp `6281234556757`, email `create2impact.id@gmail.com`). When true, `billing/page.tsx` renders WhatsApp/email contact links (pre-filled with plan name + business name via `wa.me`/`mailto:` query params) per plan card instead of the `PayButton`/Midtrans flow, so customers still have a way to pay manually while the Midtrans account clears review. The actual Midtrans integration code is untouched — this is purely a display-layer toggle in the billing page. **Flip `BILLING_MANUAL_MODE` back to `false` once Midtrans keys are confirmed working** (retry the same Sandbox-key test once the account's 2-3 business day review completes).

**Postgres gotcha hit while migrating**: `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` fails with `42P13 cannot change return type of existing function` when you add new OUT-parameter columns to a `RETURNS TABLE(...)` function (here, extending `admin_list_businesses()` with `subscription_status`/`plan_code`). Fix is `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS ... ; CREATE FUNCTION ...` instead of `CREATE OR REPLACE` — worth remembering for any future RPC signature change, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]].

content.text:
Wajar bingung, saya jelaskan strukturnya:

## Cuma ada **satu** aplikasi, tapi dua "sudut pandang" berbeda tergantung siapa yang login

**1. Akun biasa (pelanggan/pemilik toko yang daftar)**
- Login di `/login` pakai email masing-masing → masuk ke `/dashboard` → **cuma bisa lihat toko miliknya sendiri**. Tidak bisa lihat toko orang lain sama sekali (dijamin sistem, bukan sekadar disembunyikan).

**2. Akun kamu (`m.khamdannn91@gmail.com`)**
- Ini **bukan halaman terpisah** — ini akun login biasa juga, sama seperti pelanggan lain. Bedanya cuma satu: email ini sudah didaftarkan manual ke tabel khusus di database (`admins`) sejak awal, jadi akun ini punya "hak akses ekstra".
- Kalau kamu login lalu buka `/dashboard` — itu akan nunjukkin toko **milikmu sendiri** (yang mana kamu sebenarnya tidak punya toko asli, cuma dipakai buat seed akun admin).
- Untuk lihat kendali atas **semua** pengguna/toko yang terdaftar, kamu harus **buka URL terpisah**: **`kasirku-nine.vercel.app/admin`**

## Jadi halaman kontrolmu itu adalah `/admin`

Di situ kamu bisa lihat:
- Total toko terdaftar, total pemilik, transaksi hari ini
- **Daftar lengkap semua toko** yang pernah daftar — nama, jenis usaha, email pemiliknya, tanggal daftar, status langganan
- Tombol **"Tandai Sudah Bayar"** (yang baru saya buat) di tiap baris

Kalau pelanggan biasa coba buka `/admin`, mereka akan dapat halaman "tidak ditemukan" (404) — sudah saya tes sendiri, aman.

**Ringkasnya**: tidak ada 2 sistem terpisah. Satu aplikasi, satu tabel akun login — cuma akunmu ditandai spesial di database supaya kalau kamu buka `/admin`, kamu lihat semuanya; kalau orang lain buka `/admin`, ditolak.

Ada bagian yang masih membingungkan?

content.text:
Saya coba jernihkan tiga hal ini satu-satu:

## 1. "Lihat di Vercel ya?"

**Bukan** di dashboard Vercel (vercel.com) — itu cuma tempat hosting/server jalan, sama sekali beda urusan sama admin panel KasirKu. Vercel dashboard cuma buat lihat status deploy, log error server, dll — cuma kamu yang perlu lihat itu sebagai developer, pelanggan tidak pernah lihat itu sama sekali.

Yang kamu maksud (lihat semua toko + tombol Tandai Sudah Bayar) itu ada **di dalam aplikasi KasirKu sendiri**, dibuka lewat browser biasa ke:

```
kasirku-nine.vercel.app/admin
```

("vercel.app" di situ cuma alamat domainnya — karena hostingnya di Vercel — bukan berarti kamu masuk ke Vercel-nya.)

## 2. Fungsi kamu sebagai "toko"

Ini yang bikin bingung: akunmu (`m.khamdannn91@gmail.com`) **secara teknis punya `/dashboard` juga seperti pelanggan lain**, tapi kamu **tidak perlu pakai itu**. Akun itu dulu dibuat cuma buat "kunci masuk" ke `/admin`, bukan buat jualan sungguhan. Jadi:

18

22	
23	```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher

36	}

40	
41	> **Good to know**:
42	>
43	> - The `instrumentation` file should be in the root of your project and not inside the `app` or `pages` directory. If you're using the `src` folder, then place the file inside `src` alongside `pages` and `app`.
44	> - If you use the [`pageExtensions` config option](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions) to add a suffix, you will also need to update the `instrumentation` filename to match.
45

48	### Importing files with side effects
49	
50	Sometimes, it may be useful to import a file in your code because of the side effects it will cause. For example, you might import a file that defines a set of global variables, but never explicitly use the imported file in your code. You would still have access to the global variables the package has declared.

---
title: How to set up instrumentation
nav_title: Instrumentation
description: Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app
related:
  title: Learn more about Instrumentation
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/instrumentation
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

Instrumentation is the process of using code to integrate monitoring and logging tools into your application. This allows you to track the performance and behavior of your application, and to debug issues in production.

## Convention

To set up instrumentation, create `instrumentation.ts|js` file in the **root directory** of your project (or inside the [`src`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder) folder if using one).

Then, export a `register` function in the file. This function will be called **once** when a new Next.js server instance is initiated, and must complete before the server is ready to handle requests.

For example, to use Next.js with [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) and [@vercel/otel](https://vercel.com/docs/observability/otel-overview):

```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher
import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'

export function register() {
  registerOTel('next-app')
}
```

```js filename="instrumentation.js" switcher
import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'

export function register() {
  registerOTel('next-app')
}
```

See the [Next.js with OpenTelemetry example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-opentelemetry) for a complete implementation.

> **Good to know**:
>
> - The `instrumentation` file should be in the root of your project and not inside the `app` or `pages` directory. If you're using the `src` folder, then place the file inside `src` alongside `pages` and `app`.
> - If you use the [`pageExtensions` config option](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions) to add a suffix, you will also need to update the `instrumentation` filename to match.

## Examples

### Importing files with side effects

Sometimes, it may be useful to import a file in your code because of the side effects it will cause. For example, you might import a file that defines a set of global variables, but never explicitly use the imported file in your code. You would still have access to the global variables the package has declared.

We recommend importing files using JavaScript `import` syntax within your `register` function. The following example demonstrates a basic usage of `import` in a `register` function:

```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher
export async function register() {
  await import('package-with-side-effect')
}
```

```js filename="instrumentation.js" switcher
export async function register() {
  await import('package-with-side-effect')
}
```

> **Good to know:**
>
> We recommend importing the file from within the `register` function, rather than at the top of the file. By doing this, you can colocate all of your side effects in one place in your code, and avoid any unintended consequences from importing globally at the top of the file.

### Importing runtime-specific code

Next.js calls `register` in all environments, so it's important to conditionally import any code that doesn't support specific runtimes (e.g. [Edge or Node.js](/docs/app/api-reference/edge)). You can use the `NEXT_RUNTIME` environment variable to get the current environment:

```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') {
    await import('./instrumentation-node')
  }

  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {
    await import('./instrumentation-edge')
  }
}
```

```js filename="instrumentation.js" switcher
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') {
    await import('./instrumentation-node')
  }

  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {
    await import('./instrumentation-edge')
  }
}
```

1	---
2	title: instrumentation.js
3	description: API reference for the instrumentation.js file.
4	related:
5	  title: Learn more about Instrumentation
6	  links:
7	    - app/guides/instrumentation
8	---
9	
10	The `instrumentation.js|ts` file is used to integrate observability tools into your application, allowing you to track the performance and behavior, and to debug issues in production.
11	
12	To use it, place the file in the **root** of your application or inside a [`src` folder](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder) if using one.
13	
14	## Exports
15	
16	### `register` (optional)
17	
18	The file exports a `register` function that is called **once** when a new Next.js server instance is initiated, and must complete before the server is ready to handle requests. `register` can be an async function.
19	
20	```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher
21	import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'
22	
23	export function register() {
24	  registerOTel('next-app')
25	}
26	```
27	
28	```js filename="instrumentation.js" switcher
29	import { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'
30	
31	export function register() {
32	  registerOTel('next-app')
33	}
34	```
35	
36	### `onRequestError` (optional)
37	
38	You can optionally export an `onRequestError` function to track **server** errors to any custom observability provider.
39	
40	- If you're running any async tasks in `onRequestError`, make sure they're awaited. `onRequestError` will be triggered when the Next.js server captures the error.
41	- The `error` instance might not be the original error instance thrown, as it may be processed by React if encountered during Server Components rendering. If this happens, you can use `digest` property on an error to identify the actual error type.
42	
43	```ts filename="instrumentation.ts" switcher
44	import { type Instrumentation } from 'next'
45	
46	export const onRequestError: Instrumentation.onRequestError = async (
47	  err,
48	  request,
49	  context
50	) => {
51	  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
52	  const digest =
53	    typeof err === 'object' && err !== null && 'digest' in err
54	      ? String(err.digest)
55	      : undefined
56	
57	  await fetch('https://.../report-error', {
58	    method: 'POST',
59	    body: JSON.stringify({
60	      message,
61	      digest,
62	      request,
63	      context,
64	    }),
65	    headers: {
66	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
67	    },
68	  })
69	}
70	```
71	
72	```js filename="instrumentation.js" switcher
73	export async function onRequestError(err, request, context) {
74	  const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
75	  const digest =
76	    typeof err === 'object' && err !== null && 'digest' in err
77	      ? String(err.digest)
78	      : undefined
79	
80	  await fetch('https://.../report-error', {
81	    method: 'POST',
82	    body: JSON.stringify({
83	      message,
84	      digest,
85	      request,
86	      context,
87	    }),
88	    headers: {
89	      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
90	    },
91	  })
92	}
93	```
94	
95	#### Parameters
96	
97	The function accepts three parameters: `error`, `request`, and `context`.
98	
99	```ts filename="Types"
100	export function onRequestError(
101	  error: unknown,
102	  request: {
103	    path: string // resource path, e.g. /blog?name=foo
104	    method: string // request method. e.g. GET, POST, etc
105	    headers: { [key: string]: string | string[] }
106	  },
107	  context: {
108	    routerKind: 'Pages Router' | 'App Router' // the router type
109	    routePath: string // the route file path, e.g. /app/blog/[dynamic]
110	    routeType: 'render' | 'route' | 'action' | 'proxy' // the context in which the error occurred
111	    renderSource:
112	      | 'react-server-components'
113	      | 'react-server-components-payload'
114	      | 'server-rendering'
115	    revalidateReason: 'on-demand' | 'stale' | undefined // undefined is a normal request without revalidation
116	    renderType: 'dynamic' | 'dynamic-resume' // 'dynamic-resume' for PPR
117	  }
118	): void | Promise<void>
119	```
120	
121	- `error`: The caught value is typed as `unknown`. Narrow it before reading properties like `message` or `digest`.
122	- `request`: Read-only request information associated with the error.
123	- `context`: The context in which the error occurred. This can be the type of router (App or Pages Router), and/or (Server Components (`'render'`), Route Handlers (`'route'`), Server Actions (`'action'`), or Proxy (`'proxy'`)).
124	
125	### Specifying the runtime
126	
127	The `instrumentation.js` file works in both the Node.js and Edge runtime, however, you can use `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME` to target a specific runtime.
128	
129	```js filename="instrumentation.js"
130	export function register() {
131	  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {
132	    return require('./register.edge')
133	  } else {
134	    return require('./register.node')
135	  }
136	}

content.text:
Dua pertanyaan bagus, saya jawab satu-satu.

## 1. Kalau internet mati, apakah bisa jalan?

**Tidak, saat ini belum bisa.** KasirKu bergantung penuh ke Supabase (database di cloud) — setiap buka halaman kasir, tambah item, checkout, semuanya butuh koneksi internet ke server. Tidak ada penyimpanan lokal/offline sama sekali saat ini.

Ini kelemahan nyata untuk POS (biasanya wifi warung/restoran bisa putus-putus saat jam sibuk), tapi membangun mode offline (simpan transaksi lokal dulu, sinkron otomatis pas internet balik) itu **pekerjaan besar** — bukan sekadar tambahan kecil, perlu penyimpanan lokal di browser, antrian sinkronisasi, dan penanganan konflik data. Saya tidak sarankan dikerjakan sekarang, tapi bisa jadi rencana jangka menengah kalau nanti jadi keluhan serius dari pengguna.

## 2. Kasir yang lambat — saya cek kodenya

Ketemu penyebab nyata: halaman kasir (`pos/page.tsx`) melakukan **7-8 query database satu-per-satu berurutan** (bukan bersamaan) sebelum halamannya bisa muncul — ambil data toko, cek sesi kasir, ambil produk, open bill, pelanggan, metode bayar custom, self-order... semua nunggu gantian, padahal kebanyakan **tidak saling bergantung** dan bisa diambil bersamaan.

Ini kemungkinan besar penyebab lambatnya, dan ini bug yang bisa saya perbaiki — dengan menjalankan query-query yang independen itu **bersamaan** (paralel) alih-alih bergantian, harusnya waktu buka halaman kasir jauh lebih cepat.

Mau saya perbaiki sekarang?

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Parallelize independent POS page queries to cut load time

pos/page.tsx was firing 6-8 Supabase queries one after another even
though most don't depend on each other's results (products, open bills,
customers, custom payment methods, self-orders; or for ticket
businesses, categories, members, custom payment methods, today's
holiday check). Running the independent ones together via Promise.all
instead of sequentially should noticeably speed up opening the cashier
screen, which a customer flagged as sluggish.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
git push origin master

KasirKu is being developed as a SaaS-style product to be sold to other business owners (pelaku usaha) — it is not for the developer's (Melan's) own personal store. Confirmed 2026-07-08: Melan had never created an owner account in the app himself; his role is building/selling the system, not operating a store with it. Melan signed up his first real account (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com) via `/signup` on 2026-07-09, but purely to be seeded as the superadmin for `/admin` — not to operate a store. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the admin seeding details.

**Why:** changes the frame for future work — onboarding/signup flow, pricing/subscription, multi-tenant admin oversight, and marketing/landing pages matter here in a way they wouldn't for a single-owner internal tool.

**How to apply:** when working on auth, onboarding, or the root "/" experience, remember the audience is prospective *customers* signing up for the first time, not one known owner. **Update 2026-07-12 — the launch-readiness gaps below are now closed, see [[billing-midtrans]] for the biggest one:**
- `/` (`src/app/page.tsx`) is a real public marketing landing page (hero, feature grid, business-type pitch, CTA to `/signup`) — it does NOT redirect to `/dashboard`. Only redirects logged-in users away from it.
- `/admin` (superadmin panel, read-only tenant overview) has existed since 2026-07-08.
- Billing/subscription/plan-gating now exists — see [[billing-midtrans]]. A new business must pick and pay a plan before the dashboard/POS unlocks; no trial.
- Still true as a real gap: no pricing page, and prices are placeholder constants in `src/lib/billing/plans.ts` (not reviewed for real-world pricing yet).
- Still true: ToS/Privacy (`/terms`, `/privacy`) are explicitly marked as drafts not reviewed by a lawyer or checked against UU PDP — flag if asked about legal readiness.

**Known architectural gap, explicitly declined for now (2026-07-12)**: KasirKu has **no offline support** — every page (POS included) depends entirely on a live connection to Supabase, no local cache/queue/service-worker. User asked directly; told this is a large undertaking (local storage, sync queue, conflict resolution) and deliberately not started, only flagged as a possible mid-term item if it becomes a real complaint from users whose wifi drops mid-service.

**Post-launch punch list still open**: (1) auto-notify a customer (WhatsApp/email) when their subscription gets manually activated via `/admin`'s "Tandai Sudah Bayar" — proposed, user hadn't decided yet as of 2026-07-12; (2) the onboarding gap where `createBusiness` doesn't hard-limit one business per account server-side (only the UI redirect discourages a second) — flagged, not fixed, needs a decision on whether multi-business-per-account should be a real feature; (3) Sentry/error-monitoring — recommended, user said to revisit later, not started, no account created yet.
